problems.need: For Taiwan free-roaming dog population estimation, repeated dog sightings need reliable individual identity reconciliation, and a reviewed Talea survey-guide record lacks per-sighting photographs.
Surplus food donors and charities need time-bounded listings, reliable claiming, safe pickup coordination, and a way to measure recovery beyond mere collection speed.
Foodsoft's balancing screen flags false quantity mismatches when one measurement is rounded to 3 decimals and another retains full fractional precision.
Open Food Network's Canada map can center outside the service area due to outlier geocoding and fixed zoom, making legitimate nearby producers hard to locate.

repositories.capability: Foodsoft supports cooperative member order aggregation, accounting and job scheduling, including balancing/quantity computations. It is not documented as a real-time charity surplus claiming system.
Food Rescue MVP claims realtime food listings, geospatial discovery, protected claiming, pickup windows and pickup completion; no root LICENSE file was detected in the public repository.
Open Food Network is an established open-source marketplace for producers and community food hubs; its map feature is undergoing real user issue triage and bug correction.

KoboToolbox server supports offline survey collection, form management, data exports, permissions and analytics through API. It does not document photographic individual dog reconciliation or population estimation as a turnkey feature.
